Kept in this shape so the allow set can be widened entry by entry.

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerHove.capability: register a hover provider for a caller-chosen document selector; the window then asks the tab for hover markdown at a position in any matching document
MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerHove.constraint: every filter in the selector must name a scheme the tab owns (vscode-remote, untitled, vscode-notebook-cell, git); a scheme-less or '*' filter is refused, and isBuiltin must not be claimed

validator.name: documentSelectorIsTabScoped
validator.args: position 1 (selector). Accepted: a non-empty array of at most 64 plain objects, each with $serialized === true, scheme a string in {vscode-remote, untitled, vscode-notebook-cell, git}, language/notebookType string or absent, exclusive boolean or absent, isBuiltin absent or false, and pattern either absent, a string, or an object whose baseUri revives to this tab's vscode-remote authority.
denies: a string selector or any non-object entry
scheme absent, '*', or any scheme outside the allow-set (file, vscode-userdata, output, vscode-settings, vscode-chat-*, http(s))
isBuiltin === true
an empty array or more than 64 filters
a RelativePattern baseUri outside this tab's authority
anything whose shape is not recognised

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerHove.rationale: The registration is window-wide: ILanguageFeaturesService.hoverProvider.register(selector, provider) is the same registry the trusted editor consults for every model in the window, and the selector is an untrusted argument. With a scheme-less or file/vscode-userdata selector the tab is asked to render the hover for a trusted document (user settings opened in the tab window, an output channel), so its markdown is painted inside trusted UI; the hover markdown may carry command: links and https: images, and the workbench CSP allows img-src https:, which is an egress path from the trusted renderer that does not pass the tab's broker. The selector also carries isBuiltin, which LanguageFeatureRegistry uses to order providers ahead of genuine built-ins, so an unvalidated selector lets a tab outrank the real provider. Constraining the selector does not remove the hover-content risks, only the trusted-document ones.
MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerHove.activation_blocking: no - fire and forget, the proxy result is discarded and a disposable is returned synchronously (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageFeatures.ts#L2356)
open_questions: A scheme-less selector ({language:'typescript'}) is the most common ordinary form, so a pure deny costs compatibility. Rewriting a scheme-less filter to scheme:'vscode-remote' is equally safe and strictly more compatible; recommend that rewrite rather than the deny above.
Whether hover markdown is sanitised for command: links on this path, or only for trusted markdown, was not settled from the code.

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerCode.capability: register a code lens provider for a caller-chosen selector; lenses render above lines of matching documents and each carries a Command the UI executes on click

validator.name: documentSelectorIsTabScoped
validator.args: position 1 (selector), same spec as $registerHoverProvider. Position 2 (eventHandle) must be a number or undefined.
denies: as $registerHoverProvider
eventHandle neither a number nor undefined

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerCode.rationale: provideCodeLenses returns lenses verbatim from the tab and the lens command is executed by the trusted command service when the user clicks it, which is the laundering-adjacent path: the command id never passes through MainThreadCommands, so the command policy table does not see it. With an unconstrained selector the lenses are drawn on trusted documents, where a lens reading 'Run' above a line of the user's settings is indistinguishable from a built-in one. The registration itself is window-wide but the registration handle is per connection, so it cannot displace another host's registration.
open_questions: Whether a per-click confirmation or an allow-list on lens command ids is wanted; this classification assumes the command remains unfiltered on the click path.

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerComp.capability: register a completion provider for a caller-chosen selector, with trigger characters; accepted items can carry additionalTextEdits and a Command
MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerComp.constraint: same selector constraint as $registerHoverProvider; triggerCharacters must be an array of at most 64 single-character strings; extensionId is a claim and must not be used for any decision

validator.name: documentSelectorIsTabScoped
validator.args: position 1 (selector), same spec as $registerHoverProvider. Position 2 (triggerCharacters): array of at most 64 strings of length 1. Position 4 (extensionId): object with a string value field; recorded as claimedExtensionId only.
denies: as $registerHoverProvider
a triggerCharacters entry that is not a one-character string, or more than 64 of them

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerComp.rationale: A completion item's command is executed after the item is accepted, which is a weaker user gesture than a click on a link, and _inflateSuggestDto carries the tab's item verbatim into the suggest widget. An unconstrained selector lets the tab supply completions inside a trusted document, so it can propose a value the user then commits into their own settings. extensionId is only used for the debug display name and telemetry here, but it is a caller argument and must never be read as identity.
open_questions: Whether additionalTextEdits returned with an item are constrained to the document being edited was not confirmed from the code read here.

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerDocu.capability: register a link provider; returned links become clickable targets in matching documents and are opened by the trusted opener
MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerDocu.constraint: same selector constraint as $registerHoverProvider. This entry is only defensible together with a response-side check on the link url, because the url is a return value and the request filter never sees it.

validator.name: documentSelectorIsTabScoped
validator.args: position 1 (selector), same spec as $registerHoverProvider. Position 2 (supportsResolve) must be a boolean.
denies: as $registerHoverProvider
supportsResolve not a boolean

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerDocu.rationale: The link url is revived from whatever the tab returns and the links contribution opens it with allowCommands: true, so a link whose url is command:<id>?<args> executes that command on the trusted side on a single user click, with no involvement of MainThreadCommands and therefore no command-policy check. A file: url opens a host file into the window, where it becomes a text model and is then synchronised to the tab's own extension host, which closes an exfiltration loop with one click. The selector constraint limits which documents can carry such links but does nothing about the links themselves; a url check on the response is required.
open_questions: Whether the response-side url check belongs in this filter or in a patch to links.ts that drops allowCommands for links from sandboxed hosts.

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerFold.capability: register a folding range provider for a caller-chosen selector

validator.name: documentSelectorIsTabScoped
validator.args: position 1 (selector), same spec as $registerHoverProvider. Position 2 (extensionId) is a claim. Position 3 (eventHandle) must be a number or undefined.
denies: as $registerHoverProvider
eventHandle neither a number nor undefined

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerFold.rationale: The provider returns only ranges, which carry no command, no URI and no markdown, so this is the least dangerous of the six observed registrations. The residual capability is that the tab learns when a matching document is viewed and can collapse regions of it; with an unconstrained selector that includes trusted documents. Folding a region of a document the user is reading is a presentation attack worth bounding but not a reachability grant.

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerCode.capability: register a code action provider; resolved actions carry a WorkspaceEdit the trusted bulk-edit service applies and a Command the trusted command service runs
MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerCode.constraint: same selector constraint as $registerHoverProvider, plus metadata.providedKinds and documentation bounded (at most 64 kinds, at most 64 documentation entries, strings at most 256 bytes). As with document links this is only defensible once the returned edit is checked response-side: the request filter cannot see it.

validator.name: documentSelectorIsTabScoped
validator.args: position 1 (selector), same spec as $registerHoverProvider. Position 2 (metadata): plain object; providedKinds absent or an array of at most 64 strings of at most 256 bytes; documentation absent or an array of at most 64 {kind,command,title} objects. Position 4 (extensionId) is a claim, recorded only. Position 5 (supportsResolve) must be a boolean.
denies: as $registerHoverProvider
metadata not a plain object, or either bound exceeded
supportsResolve not a boolean

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$registerCode.rationale: resolveCodeAction takes the tab's reply, revives it with reviveWorkspaceEditDto and the editor then hands that edit to IBulkEditService.apply, so a code action the user triggers from the lightbulb can write, create, rename or delete any resource the edit names, including file: resources on the host. The documentation and displayName fields are rendered in the lightbulb menu, so the attacker also chooses what the action claims to be. Constraining the selector keeps the lightbulb out of trusted documents but does not constrain the edit, which is the dangerous half.
open_questions: Whether bulk edits originating from a sandboxed host should be scoped to the tab authority in IBulkEditService itself; that would cover code actions, rename, paste edits and inline completions in one place.

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$unregister.capability: dispose one of this connection's own language feature registrations by handle
MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$unregister.rationale: The handle is looked up in this MainThreadLanguageFeatures instance's own DisposableMap, and there is one instance per extension host connection, so a tab can only dispose registrations it made. Numbers it has not used are a no-op. Denying it would leak registrations for the life of the window.

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$emitCodeLens.capability: fire this connection's own code lens change emitter
MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$emitCodeLens.rationale: The eventHandle is resolved in the connection's own registration map and the call only fires if the entry is an Emitter, so an unknown or wrong-typed handle is a no-op. The effect is that the editor re-asks the tab for lenses on documents the tab's own selector matches. The only abuse is call volume, which is a general rate concern rather than a capability.
MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$emitCodeLens.activation_blocking: no - fire and forget from an event handler (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageFeatures.ts#L2291)

MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$emitFoldingR.capability: fire this connection's own folding range change emitter
MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$emitFoldingR.rationale: Identical shape to $emitCodeLensEvent: handle-scoped lookup in the connection's own map, Emitter type check, no arguments that reach a service. The companion of $registerFoldingRangeProvider, which an ordinary provider with onDidChangeFoldingRanges calls.
MainThreadLanguageFeatures.$emitFoldingR.activation_blocking: no - fire and forget from an event handler

MainThreadDecorations.$registerDecoratio.capability: register a window-wide decorations provider; the window then asks the tab to decorate every resource it renders, whatever its scheme
MainThreadDecorations.$registerDecoratio.constraint: label must be a plain string of at most 100 characters with no control characters; the residual URI disclosure is not fixable from the arguments and needs a trusted-side scheme filter on provideDecorations

validator.name: decorationProviderLabel
validator.args: position 0 (handle) must be a number; position 1 (label) must be a string of at most 100 characters containing no C0 control characters and no markdown link syntax.
denies: a non-number handle
a non-string label, a label over 100 characters, or one containing control characters

MainThreadDecorations.$registerDecoratio.rationale: The provider is registered with the window's IDecorationsService, so provideDecorations is called with the URI of any resource the window decorates, not only the tab's: if the user opens settings or another host-scheme resource in a tab window, that URI is queued and sent to the tab. Only the URI travels, not the content, so this is path disclosure rather than a read. The returned DecorationData sets a letter, colour and tooltip on explorer and tab entries, which is a small spoofing surface, and the label is shown in the decoration settings UI. The arguments carry nothing else, so an argument validator can only bound the label.
open_questions: Whether the queue should drop requests whose URI is not in the tab's authority before they reach the tab; that is the only way to close the path disclosure.

MainThreadDecorations.$onDidChange.capability: tell the window that decorations changed for a list of resources
MainThreadDecorations.$onDidChange.constraint: every element of the resources array must revive to this tab's vscode-remote authority or to untitled:

validator.name: seclabUriArgs
validator.args: position 1 is already declared in SECLAB_URI_ARGS as a UriComponents position and the extractor flattens arrays element by element, so each entry is checked individually.
denies: any element that is not URI components
any element outside this tab's authority

MainThreadDecorations.$onDidChange.rationale: The handle is resolved in the connection's own provider map, so a tab can only fire its own emitter, and the only payload is the URI list, which the existing positional rule already constrains. Firing for a URI outside the tab would make the window re-query decorations for a trusted resource, which the URI rule prevents. The remaining concern is call volume.

MainThreadDecorations.$unregisterDecorat.capability: dispose this connection's own decoration provider by handle
MainThreadDecorations.$unregisterDecorat.rationale: The handle is looked up in this instance's own map, so only the tab's own registrations are reachable; an unknown handle is a no-op. It is the immediate lifecycle counterpart of $registerDecorationProvider.

MainThreadDocumentContentProviders.$regi.capability: become the content provider for an arbitrary URI scheme in the trusted window
MainThreadDocumentContentProviders.$regi.constraint: the scheme must be a lowercase token the tab owns; schemes the trusted side already serves, and the vscode-* family, are refused

validator.name: textContentProviderScheme
validator.args: position 0 (handle) must be a number; position 1 (scheme) must be a string of at most 64 characters matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*$ and must not be in the reserved set {file, vscode-userdata, vscode-remote, untitled, output, inmemory, http, https, data, command, mailto, comments-input, conflictResolution, vscode-settings} nor start with 'vscode' nor with 'seclab'. The filter is additionally given a snapshot predicate, taken before any sandboxed host attaches, of the schemes the trusted side has already registered a content provider for; a hit is denied. If that snapshot is unavailable the validator denies.
denies: a scheme that is not a plain lowercase token
any reserved or vscode-prefixed scheme
any scheme already served on the trusted side
an unavailable snapshot (fail closed)

MainThreadDocumentContentProviders.$regi.rationale: registerTextModelContentProvider unshifts the new provider to the front of the list for that scheme, so the most recent registration wins, and the resolver consults providers for any scheme the file service does not serve. file: and vscode-userdata: are safe only because the file-service branch is taken first; output: is not, so a tab registering 'output' would serve the content the Output panel displays, including the Tab Manager's channel, which is the first place an operator looks when a tab misbehaves. The provider also learns every URI of its scheme that the window resolves. Duplicates are not refused upstream, so without a validator this is a shadowing primitive.
open_questions: The git extension runs workspace-kind inside the tab and registers scheme 'git'; the reserved list above must stay in step with whatever the trusted side registers, so the snapshot predicate is the load-bearing half.

MainThreadDocumentContentProviders.$unre.capability: dispose this connection's own text content provider by handle
MainThreadDocumentContentProviders.$unre.rationale: Handle-scoped delete on this instance's own DisposableMap; an unknown handle is a no-op. Immediate counterpart of $registerTextContentProvider.

MainThreadDocumentContentProviders.$onVi.capability: replace the full text of any model in the window identified by URI
MainThreadDocumentContentProviders.$onVi.constraint: the URI must revive to this tab's vscode-remote authority or untitled:

validator.name: seclabUriArgs
validator.args: position 0 is already declared in SECLAB_URI_ARGS.
denies: any URI outside this tab's authority

MainThreadDocumentContentProviders.$onVi.rationale: The method looks the model up by URI in the window's model service, with no check that the caller provided that model, and applies edits to it, so without the URI rule a tab could rewrite the in-memory text of any open document, including a host file the user is editing. With the rule it can still rewrite any model inside its own authority, which is content it already controls. The edit is in-memory; persisting it needs a save.
MainThreadDocumentContentProviders.$onVi.activation_blocking: no - returned into an event handler (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostDocumentContentProviders.ts#L81)

MainThreadDocuments.$tryOpenDocument.capability: resolve a URI into a text model the window holds a reference to, and so into the tab's document set
MainThreadDocuments.$tryOpenDocument.constraint: the URI must revive to this tab's vscode-remote authority or untitled:

validator.name: seclabUriArgs
validator.args: position 0 is already declared in SECLAB_URI_ARGS.
denies: file:, vscode-userdata: or any other authority than this tab's

MainThreadDocuments.$tryOpenDocument.rationale: The default branch hands the URI to ITextModelService.createModelReference, which for any scheme the file service serves resolves the real bytes; with file: or vscode-userdata: that is a host read, and the resulting model is immediately synchronised to the calling extension host, so the content lands in the tab. The URI rule is exactly what removes that. The untitled branch is separate: it calls toLocalResource and probes existence before creating, which is the one place a non-tab path could still be touched.
MainThreadDocuments.$tryOpenDocument.activation_blocking: yes for the API call - openTextDocument returns this promise, so a rejection rejects workspace.openTextDocument and fails activation if an extension awaits it in activate() (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostDocuments.ts#L90)
open_questions: With an untitled: URI carrying a path, _handleUntitledScheme calls toLocalResource(uri, remoteAuthority, defaultUriScheme) and fileService.exists on the result. If a tab window's IWorkbenchEnvironmentService.remoteAuthority is ever unset, that maps to file: and becomes a host existence probe. Not settled from the code here.

MainThreadDocuments.$trySaveDocument.capability: save a text document by URI

validator.name: seclabUriArgs
validator.args: position 0 is already declared in SECLAB_URI_ARGS.
denies: any URI outside this tab's authority

MainThreadDocuments.$trySaveDocument.rationale: ITextFileService.save writes the model's current contents to the resource, so without the URI rule a tab that had got a trusted model into the window could persist its edits to a host path. Constrained to the tab's own authority it writes only inside the sandbox's workspace, which the tab already controls. It is the immediate counterpart of $tryOpenDocument in the document lifecycle.
MainThreadDocuments.$trySaveDocument.activation_blocking: no for activation; the promise is returned to TextDocument.save

MainThreadDocuments.$tryCreateDocument.capability: create an untitled document with caller-chosen language and content
MainThreadDocuments.$tryCreateDocument.constraint: options must be a plain object; language at most 64 characters, content at most 5 MiB, encoding from the known set

validator.name: untitledDocumentOptions
validator.args: position 0 (options) absent or a plain object with only the keys language, content, encoding; language a string of at most 64 characters; content a string of at most 5 MiB; encoding a string of at most 32 characters.
denies: an unknown key
content over the bound
a non-object options value

MainThreadDocuments.$tryCreateDocument.rationale: No URI is involved: the untitled model is created from scratch, so there is no host reach. The arguments are unbounded strings that become an in-memory model and a visible editor, so the only concerns are memory and a document whose contents the tab chose being presented as the user's own untitled buffer. Bounding the content keeps the memory cost of one call finite.
MainThreadDocuments.$tryCreateDocument.activation_blocking: no for activation; the promise is returned to workspace.openTextDocument({content})

MainThreadTextEditors.$tryShowTextDocume.capability: open an editor on a URI in the window and return its editor id
MainThreadTextEditors.$tryShowTextDocume.constraint: the URI must revive to this tab's vscode-remote authority or untitled:

validator.name: seclabUriArgs
validator.args: position 0 is already declared in SECLAB_URI_ARGS. Position 1 (options) should additionally be a plain object; preserveFocus and pinned booleans, position a number.
denies: any URI outside this tab's authority

MainThreadTextEditors.$tryShowTextDocume.rationale: IEditorService.openEditor on an unconstrained URI would open a host file in the window, and an opened model is synchronised to the tab's extension host, so this is a read primitive as much as a UI one; the URI rule removes it. What remains is that a tab can take the active editor and move focus in its own window at will, which is noise and a nuisance rather than a boundary crossing. The returned editor id names an editor over the tab's own resource.
MainThreadTextEditors.$tryShowTextDocume.activation_blocking: yes for the API call - awaited, so window.showTextDocument rejects (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTextEditors.ts#L85)
open_questions: Opening editors is also a focus-stealing surface; whether the tab should be rate limited here is a UX decision, not settled from the code.

MainThreadTextEditors.$registerTextEdito.capability: register a decoration type whose render options are turned into CSS in the trusted window, including url() values built from caller URIs
MainThreadTextEditors.$registerTextEdito.constraint: every URI anywhere in the render options (gutterIconPath, contentIconPath, and the same keys inside light, dark, before and after) must revive to this tab's vscode-remote authority; http and https are refused

validator.name: decorationRenderOptionsUris
validator.args: position 2 (options) must be a plain object no deeper than 8 levels. The validator walks the fixed key paths options[.light|.dark][.before|.after].{gutterIconPath,contentIconPath} plus the top-level gutterIconPath and contentIconPath. Each value present must be URI components whose scheme is vscode-remote and whose authority equals this tab's authority. Position 0 (extensionId) is a claim, recorded only. Position 1 (key) must be a string of at most 128 characters.
denies: any icon path with scheme http, https, file, vscode-userdata or any authority other than this tab's
an icon path that is a string rather than URI components
an options object deeper than 8 levels or containing a getter-like non-plain value
any unrecognised shape in a checked position

MainThreadTextEditors.$registerTextEdito.rationale: The protocol types this parameter as IDecorationRenderOptions, not UriComponents, so the extracted SECLAB_URI_ARGS table has no entry for it and the positional rule does not apply; the URIs are nested. abstractCodeEditorService revives those paths and formats them straight into CSS background and content url() rules. The workbench CSP allows img-src https:, so an https icon path is fetched by the trusted renderer, outside the tab's sandbox and outside its broker, which makes an arbitrary-length URL path an egress channel. The decoration key is prefixed with the connection's instance id, so cross-host key collision is not reachable.
MainThreadTextEditors.$registerTextEdito.activation_blocking: no - fire and forget from window.createTextEditorDecorationType (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTextEditor.ts#L28)
open_questions: Whether other render-option fields (contentText, fontStyle) can carry a url() through CSS injection was not examined; the formatter escapes values through strings.format, which was not audited here.

MainThreadTextEditors.$removeTextEditorD.capability: remove a decoration type this connection registered
MainThreadTextEditors.$removeTextEditorD.rationale: The key is prefixed with this MainThreadTextEditors instance's id before lookup, and there is one instance per extension host connection, so only this tab's own decoration types are reachable. The immediate counterpart of $registerTextEditorDecorationType.

MainThreadTreeViews.$registerTreeViewDat.capability: become the data provider for any tree view registered in the window, including one contributed by a UI-side extension
MainThreadTreeViews.$registerTreeViewDat.constraint: treeViewId must name a view contributed by an extension running in this tab

validator.name: treeViewOwnedByTab
validator.args: position 0 (treeViewId) must be a string of at most 256 characters that the injected predicate ownsView(tabId, treeViewId) accepts. ownsView is built from the extension registry: it returns true only when the view with that id was contributed by an extension that is running in this tab (its resolved extension location is this tab's remote authority). The predicate is evaluated at call time, after whenInstalledExtensionsRegistered, and returns false when the registry cannot answer.
denies: a view id contributed by a UI-side extension or by the workbench itself
a view id that is not in the registry
a non-string or over-long id
any call where the predicate cannot be evaluated (fail closed)

MainThreadTreeViews.$registerTreeViewDat.rationale: getTreeView resolves the id straight out of the global ViewsRegistry with no check that the caller contributed that view, so a tab can set viewer.dataProvider for a view belonging to the trusted local extension host and own what that view shows. Tree items are then supplied by the tab: label, description and tooltip are rendered as the view's content, iconPath becomes an image URL in the trusted renderer (CSP img-src allows https:), resourceUri decides what the row points at, and a tree item's command is executed by the trusted command service when the row is clicked. Scoping the view id to the tab's own extensions is what keeps this inside the tab's own UI.
MainThreadTreeViews.$registerTreeViewDat.activation_blocking: no at creation - the promise is kept and only awaited later by reveal (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTreeViews.ts#L98 and #L152)
open_questions: Whether a tab can contribute a view into a UI-side container (and so place its tree next to trusted views) depends on the views contribution point, which was not read here.

MainThreadTreeViews.$disposeTree.capability: clear the data provider and drag-and-drop controller of a tree view by id

validator.name: treeViewOwnedByTab
validator.args: position 0 (treeViewId) must be a string of at most 256 characters that the injected predicate ownsView(tabId, treeViewId) accepts. ownsView is built from the extension registry: it returns true only when the view with that id was contributed by an extension that is running in this tab (its resolved extension location is this tab's remote authority). The predicate is evaluated at call time, after whenInstalledExtensionsRegistered, and returns false when the registry cannot answer.
denies: a view id contributed by a UI-side extension or by the workbench itself
a view id that is not in the registry
a non-string or over-long id
any call where the predicate cannot be evaluated (fail closed)

MainThreadTreeViews.$disposeTree.rationale: The id is resolved through the same unchecked getTreeView, and the method sets dataProvider and dragAndDropController to undefined, so without the ownership check a tab can blank any view in the window, including a UI-side extension's. The same validator covers it, and for views the tab owns the call is the ordinary dispose path.

MainThreadTreeViews.$refresh.capability: refresh items of a tree view by id
MainThreadTreeViews.$refresh.constraint: same ownership constraint as $registerTreeViewDataProvider, plus at most 1024 handles per call

validator.name: treeViewOwnedByTab
validator.args: position 0 (treeViewId) must be a string of at most 256 characters that the injected predicate ownsView(tabId, treeViewId) accepts. ownsView is built from the extension registry: it returns true only when the view with that id was contributed by an extension that is running in this tab (its resolved extension location is this tab's remote authority). The predicate is evaluated at call time, after whenInstalledExtensionsRegistered, and returns false when the registry cannot answer. Position 1 (itemsToRefreshByHandle) must be a plain object with at most 1024 own keys.
denies: a view id contributed by a UI-side extension or by the workbench itself
a view id that is not in the registry
a non-string or over-long id
any call where the predicate cannot be evaluated (fail closed)
more than 1024 handles in one call

MainThreadTreeViews.$refresh.rationale: The method only acts when the connection also has a data provider registered for that id, so the ownership check on registration already limits it, but applying the same validator keeps the two in step and bounds the work one call can schedule. It is the call an ordinary tree data provider makes on every onDidChangeTreeData.

MainThreadTreeViews.$setMessage.capability: set the message shown in a tree view
MainThreadTreeViews.$setMessage.constraint: same ownership constraint, plus the message must be a string or a markdown string of at most 1024 characters

validator.name: treeViewOwnedByTab
validator.args: position 0 (treeViewId) must be a string of at most 256 characters that the injected predicate ownsView(tabId, treeViewId) accepts. ownsView is built from the extension registry: it returns true only when the view with that id was contributed by an extension that is running in this tab (its resolved extension location is this tab's remote authority). The predicate is evaluated at call time, after whenInstalledExtensionsRegistered, and returns false when the registry cannot answer. Position 1 (message) must be a string of at most 1024 characters, or a plain object whose value is such a string.
denies: a view id contributed by a UI-side extension or by the workbench itself
a view id that is not in the registry
a non-string or over-long id
any call where the predicate cannot be evaluated (fail closed)
a message over 1024 characters
a message object with keys other than value, isTrusted, supportThemeIcons, supportHtml
isTrusted set to true

MainThreadTreeViews.$setMessage.rationale: The message is rendered inside the view, and a markdown message with isTrusted would let command links through, so the validator refuses that field outright. With the ownership check the text appears only in the tab's own view, where tab-chosen text is expected and is presented as tab data.

MainThreadTreeViews.$setTitle.capability: set the title and description of a tree view
MainThreadTreeViews.$setTitle.constraint: same ownership constraint, plus title and description bounded to 256 characters of plain text

validator.name: treeViewOwnedByTab
validator.args: position 0 (treeViewId) must be a string of at most 256 characters that the injected predicate ownsView(tabId, treeViewId) accepts. ownsView is built from the extension registry: it returns true only when the view with that id was contributed by an extension that is running in this tab (its resolved extension location is this tab's remote authority). The predicate is evaluated at call time, after whenInstalledExtensionsRegistered, and returns false when the registry cannot answer. Position 1 (title) must be a string of at most 256 characters; position 2 (description) a string of at most 256 characters or undefined.
denies: a view id contributed by a UI-side extension or by the workbench itself
a view id that is not in the registry
a non-string or over-long id
any call where the predicate cannot be evaluated (fail closed)
a title or description over 256 characters, or containing control characters

MainThreadTreeViews.$setTitle.rationale: Without the ownership check this renames a trusted view, which is a direct impersonation surface in the sidebar. Scoped to the tab's own views it is the ordinary TreeView.title setter. The bound keeps a long title from distorting the layout of the surrounding trusted chrome.

MainThreadStatusBar.$setEntry.capability: create or update a status bar entry in the window, by an id the caller chooses, with caller-chosen text, tooltip and command
MainThreadStatusBar.$setEntry.constraint: entryId must be namespaced to an extension running in this tab, never a bare generated number and never a first-party id; the claimed extensionId must be discarded in favour of the connection-bound identity; command.id must be a command the policy table marks reachable; text and tooltip bounded and non-trusted markdown

validator.name: statusBarEntryOwnedByTab
validator.args: position 0 (entryId) must be a string of at most 256 characters matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\.[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$ whose extension-id part is an extension running in this tab (same ownsExtension predicate as treeViewOwnedByTab) and is not in the trusted first-party set {seclab.tab-manager, vscode.github-authentication, vscode.microsoft-authentication}. Position 2 (extensionId) must equal the connection-bound identity or be undefined. Position 3 (name) and position 4 (text) must be strings of at most 256 characters. Position 5 (tooltip) must be a string of at most 1024 characters, or a markdown object without isTrusted. Position 7 (command) must be absent or a plain object whose id is a string the policy table marks reachable for this tab. Positions 8 and 9 (color, backgroundColor) must be a string or a {id} object. Position 11 (priority) must be a finite number.
denies: a bare numeric entryId, which is what an anonymous createStatusBarItem produces and is trivially guessable across hosts
an entryId whose extension part is a first-party or non-tab extension
a claimed extensionId that differs from the connection identity
a tooltip markdown object with isTrusted
a command id that is not reachable, including anything with the seclab. prefix
any unrecognised shape in a checked position

MainThreadStatusBar.$setEntry.rationale: ExtensionStatusBarItemService is a window singleton shared by both extension hosts, and setOrUpdateEntry keys purely on the caller-supplied entryId: an existing entry is updated in place, so a tab that names another host's id takes over that entry's text, colour, tooltip and command. Anonymous entries get ids that are plain incrementing integers, so '1' collides with the first anonymous entry of the local extension host without any guessing. The entry's command is executed by the trusted command service on click, which is a command path that never passes through MainThreadCommands, and the claimed extensionId feeds the priority hash and the Manage Extension action. Identity therefore has to come from the connection, which is why this is constrained rather than allowed.
MainThreadStatusBar.$setEntry.activation_blocking: no - fire and forget from the throttled update (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostStatusBar.ts#L301)
open_questions: A rewrite that prefixes entryId with the tab id on both $setEntry and $disposeEntry would be transparent to the extension host and would remove the collision class entirely; it is preferable to the deny above and should be considered instead.

The constructor pushes every existing entry in the window to the attaching host via $acceptStaticEntries, which hands a tab the exact ids, text and command of the trusted entries. That is a push surface, not covered here.

MainThreadStatusBar.$disposeEntry.capability: dispose a status bar entry this connection defined
MainThreadStatusBar.$disposeEntry.rationale: The lookup is in this MainThreadStatusBar instance's own _entryDisposables map, which only receives an entry when setOrUpdateEntry reported DidDefine for this connection, so another host's entry is not reachable even by naming its id. An unknown id is a no-op. Denying it would leave the tab's entries in the status bar for the life of the window.
open_questions: If the $setEntry prefix rewrite is adopted, the same rewrite must be applied here so the ids stay symmetric.

a backing file outside this tab's authority

MainThreadOutputService.$register.rationale: The channel id is built by string concatenation from the caller's extensionId and label, and the registry ignores a duplicate id rather than rejecting it, so a tab that registers the id a UI-side extension will later use squats that channel and the real extension's output silently goes nowhere. The channel's source resource is read by the Output view, so without the positional URI rule a file: resource would render host file contents in the panel. The label is shown in the channel picker, where 'Git' or 'seclab Tab Manager' from a tab is indistinguishable from the real one.

validator.name: progressOptions
validator.args: position 0 (handle) a number. Position 1 (options) a plain object: location must be one of 1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, or a string view id that ownsView accepts for this tab; title a string of at most 200 characters; source absent or {label,id} strings of at most 128 characters each; cancellable a boolean; telemetryId and notificationId must be absent. When location is 15 (Notification) the title must not match /\]\(/ and must contain no C0 control characters. Position 2 (extensionId) must equal the connection-bound identity or be undefined.
denies: an unknown numeric location or a view id the tab does not own
a Notification title containing markdown link syntax
telemetryId or notificationId present
a claimed extensionId that differs from the connection identity, which is what selects URGENT priority for the two authentication extensions
any unrecognised shape

MainThreadProgress.$startProgress.rationale: With ProgressLocation.Notification the title becomes a notification message, progressService runs parseLinkedText over it for extension-sourced progress, and the notification renderer opens a clicked link with allowCommands: true, so a title of the form [Retry](command:<id>) is one user click from executing a trusted-side command without passing MainThreadCommands. extensionId is an argument and is compared against URGENT_PROGRESS_SOURCES, so a tab naming vscode.github-authentication gets an urgent, sticky notification and a Manage Extension action attributed to that extension. The notification itself is window chrome, so arbitrary text there impersonates trusted UI regardless of the link question.
MainThreadProgress.$startProgress.activation_blocking: no - the proxy call is explicitly .catch(onUnexpectedExternalError) and withProgress resolves on the ext host's own task (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostProgress.ts#L43)

validator.name: progressMessageIsPlainText
validator.args: position 0 (handle) a number. Position 1 (message) a plain object whose message, if present, is a string of at most 200 characters not matching /\]\(/ and free of C0 control characters, and whose increment, if present, is a finite number between 0 and 100.

a non-finite or out-of-range increment

MainThreadProgress.$progressReport.rationale: The handle is resolved in this connection's own map, so only the tab's own progress is reachable, but the reported message is rendered in the same notification that parses linked text, so the link check belongs here too or the constraint on $startProgress is trivially bypassed by reporting the link afterwards. MainThreadProgress.$progressEnd.rationale: Looks the handle up in this connection's own map, resolves the task and deletes the entry; an unknown handle is a no-op and no other host's progress is addressable. MainThreadSCM.$registerSourceControl.capability: register a source control provider in the window, with a root, an icon and a document that backs its input box
MainThreadSCM.$registerSourceControl.constraint: rootUri and inputBoxDocumentUri must be under this tab's authority (already enforced positionally) and the iconPath, which is not, must be too

validator.args: Position 4 (rootUri) and position 7 (inputBoxDocumentUri) are already in SECLAB_URI_ARGS. Position 5 (iconPath) must be absent, a ThemeIcon object {id} with id a string of at most 128 characters, URI components under this tab's vscode-remote authority, or a {light,dark} pair of such URI components. Position 2 (id) and position 3 (label) must be strings of at most 256 characters.

an iconPath shape that is neither ThemeIcon, URI components, nor a light/dark pair
an over-long id or label

MainThreadSCM.$registerSourceControl.rationale: inputBoxDocumentUri is passed to ITextModelService.createModelReference, so without the positional rule a host file would be resolved and then synchronised to the tab; that position is covered. iconPath is position 5 and is typed as a union, so the extractor did not record it and the positional rule does not apply: an https icon is rendered by the trusted window and the CSP allows img-src https:, which is egress that does not pass the broker. validator.args: Position 0 (handle) a number. Position 1 (features) a plain object restricted to the declared keys. hasArtifactProvider, hasHistoryProvider, hasQuickDiffProvider, hasSecondaryQuickDiffProvider booleans; count a finite number between 0 and 1e6; quickDiffLabel, secondaryQuickDiffLabel, commitTemplate, contextValue, activeRepositoryName strings of at most 1024 characters; acceptInputCommand absent or a plain command object whose id is reachable; actionButton absent, null, or {command, secondaryCommands, enabled} where every command is such an object and secondaryCommands is at most 8 arrays of at most 16 commands; statusBarCommands absent or an array of at most 16 such commands.

an unknown key in features
an array longer than its bound
a commitTemplate or label over 1024 characters

MainThreadSCM.$updateSourceControl.rationale: statusBarCommands are rendered in the window's status bar next to trusted entries and are executed by the trusted command service when clicked, so an unvalidated command id here is the same laundering-adjacent path as a status bar entry's command, reached without naming an entry id. actionButton and acceptInputCommand are the same shape in the SCM view, and commitTemplate pre-fills the commit message the user may then commit. a raw resource that is not the expected 10-tuple
a command id that is not reachable
any count over the bounds above
any unrecognised shape

validator.name: scmResourceSplicesAreTabScoped
validator.args: The splices argument (position 2 of $registerGroups, position 1 of $spliceResourceStates) must be an array of at most 64 [groupHandle, groupSlices] pairs, groupHandle a number, groupSlices an array of at most 256 [start, deleteCount, rawResources] triples with finite non-negative numbers and rawResources an array of at most 4096 entries. MainThreadSCM.$spliceResourceStates.rationale: The URIs here are nested inside SCMRawResourceSplices rather than being top-level UriComponents parameters, so the extracted positional rule does not cover them at all: $spliceResourceStates has no SECLAB_URI_ARGS entry. MainThreadSCM.$unregisterGroup.rationale: Both the source control and the group are resolved through this connection's own maps, and a missing entry returns early, so the reach is the tab's own SCM state. It is the ordinary disposal path for a resource group.

cross_cutting: Document sync dominates every selector constraint in this group. MainThreadDocumentsAndEditors synchronises every text model in the window to every attached extension host, filtered only by shouldSynchronizeModel, which checks size and simple-widget and nothing else: no scheme check at all. One instance is created per extension host connection, so a tab window's remote host receives the content of any vscode-userdata:, file: or output: document the user opens in that window. That is a push (ExtHostDocuments.$acceptDocumentsAndEditorsDelta), not a MainThread* call, so this filter cannot see it; it needs its own control. Until it has one, a selector constraint stops a tab injecting content into a trusted document but does not stop it reading one. Evidence: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a717861c07586a53d83b80d742cd3f59b20a6273/src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadDocumentsAndEditors.ts#L165-L200 and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a717861c07586a53d83b80d742cd3f59b20a6273/src/vs/editor/common/model.ts#L1624-L1628.

The filter screens requests, not responses. Every registration in this group turns into a trusted-side call into the tab whose RETURN value is revived and acted on without passing the filter: code action WorkspaceEdits (applied by IBulkEditService), document link urls, completion items, tree items, SCM resource rows, timeline items. The verdicts above constrain who may be asked and about what; they cannot constrain what comes back. $registerCodeActionSupport and $registerDocumentLinkProvider are only defensible once a response-side check exists, and that is stated in their entries.

User-click command execution bypasses the command policy table. A Command carried in a code lens, a code action, a status bar entry, a tree item, an SCM status bar command or an action button is executed by the trusted ICommandService on click; a command: URL in a document link is executed by the opener with allowCommands: true (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a717861c07586a53d83b80d742cd3f59b20a6273/src/vs/editor/contrib/links/browser/links.ts#L253), and the same is true of a link in a progress notification message (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a717861c07586a53d83b80d742cd3f59b20a6273/src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/notifications/notificationsViewer.ts#L466). None of these paths goes through MainThreadCommands.$executeCommand, so the commands.exact table does not see them. Either the command ids in these payloads are checked where they are supplied, or the click paths are patched; the validators above assume the former.

https: URLs rendered by the trusted window are an egress channel that does not pass the tab's broker. The workbench CSP allows img-src https: (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a717861c07586a53d83b80d742cd3f59b20a6273/src/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html#L11-L18), and tab-supplied URIs reach image and CSS url() positions through decoration render options, SCM provider and history-ref icons, tree item icons and markdown images in hovers and tooltips. An attacker-chosen path component is enough to carry data out. Every validator in this group that touches an icon position therefore refuses http and https, not only foreign authorities.

SECLAB_URI_ARGS only covers parameters typed exactly UriComponents in extHost.protocol.ts, so union-typed and nested URIs are invisible to the positional rule. Three cases are in this group alone: MainThreadSCM.$registerSourceControl position 5 (iconPath, union-typed; the table records only [4,7]), MainThreadSCM.$spliceResourceStates (no entry at all; the URIs are inside SCMRawResourceSplices), and MainThreadTextEditors.$registerTextEditorDecorationType (URIs inside IDecorationRenderOptions). A sweep of the protocol for union-typed and nested URI positions is warranted, because an entry whose constraint reads 'the URI rule suffices' would be wrong wherever one was missed.

Caller-named ids with no ownership check recur across the group: tree view ids (ViewsRegistry, mainThreadTreeViews.ts#L214-L217), output channel ids (window-wide IOutputService), status bar entry ids (a window singleton shared by both extension hosts, with anonymous ids being bare integers), and timeline provider ids (TimelineService explicitly allows overwriting a duplicate). These registries are renderer-realm singletons, so the reach is within one window rather than across tabs, but the trusted local extension host -- the Tab Manager and the auth providers -- lives in that same window. That is why four separate ownership validators appear above; they are one pattern, and a shared ownsExtension/ownsView predicate should implement all of them.

Several of those ids are evidence surfaces. MainThreadOutputService.$dispose, $update and $close reach any channel in the window by id, and MainThreadTreeViews.$disposeTree blanks any view, so an unconstrained tab can silence the 'seclab Tab Manager' output channel -- the first place AGENTS.md section 7 says to look when a tab misbehaves -- or the UI that shows it. That is adjacent to the rpc-filter-log-is-trustworthy invariant, which today rests on MainThreadLogger being denied and $writeFile being authority-constrained; it does not currently mention output channels.

Extension identity arrives as an argument on several methods here: $setEntry position 2, $startProgress position 2 (compared against URGENT_PROGRESS_SOURCES to grant urgent notification priority), MainThreadOutputService.$register position 3 (it becomes the channel id), plus $registerCodeActionSupport and $registerCompletionsProvider where it is only a display name. Per the identity-never-from-arguments invariant these should be flagged identity_from_argument and rewritten to the connection-bound identity rather than validated, which the drift check will enforce as deny-or-rewrite.

MainThreadSCM registers a text model content provider for the vscode-scm scheme per extension host context, and registerTextModelContentProvider unshifts, so the most recently attached host is asked first for that scheme. A tab's host attaching after the local one therefore takes precedence for vscode-scm documents by construction, without calling anything this table covers. Evidence: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a717861c07586a53d83b80d742cd3f59b20a6273/src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadSCM.ts#L69-L80 and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a717861c07586a53d83b80d742cd3f59b20a6273/src/vs/workbench/services/textmodelResolver/common/textModelResolverService.ts#L163-L172.

Two pushes in this group hand a tab the information it needs to attack the ids above: MainThreadStatusBar's constructor sends every existing status bar entry in the window, with its entryId, text, tooltip and command, to the attaching host ($acceptStaticEntries, mainThreadStatusBar.ts#L30-L41), and MainThreadOutputService pushes the visible channel id. Neither is a MainThread* call, so neither is covered here; they belong in the push inventory.

No instruction-like text aimed at an agent was found in any file read for this classification. The upstream comments encountered (for example the TimelineService comment explaining why duplicate registration is allowed) are ordinary developer commentary and were treated as data, not as direction.

MainThreadFileSystem.$ensureActivation.capability: make the window activate any file system provider scheme, firing onFileSystem:<scheme> activation events in every extension host of the window
MainThreadFileSystem.$ensureActivation.constraint: scheme must be a single well-formed URI scheme token; no other shape is accepted

validator.name: fileSystemSchemeIsWellFormed
validator.args: arg0 (scheme): must be a string of length 1..64 matching /^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*$/ after no normalisation (the value is passed verbatim to IFileService.activateProvider and then concatenated into the activation event id)
denies: non-string arg0
empty string
strings longer than 64 chars
any character outside the RFC 3986 scheme set, including ':' '/' whitespace and control characters, which would otherwise forge an activation event id
extra arguments beyond arg0

MainThreadFileSystem.$ensureActivation.rationale: IFileService.activateProvider returns immediately when a provider for the scheme already exists, so the trusted file:/vscode-userdata providers are unaffected. For an unregistered scheme it fires _onWillActivateFileSystemProvider, whose workbench listener activates extensions by the event onFileSystem:<scheme> — in the local UI extension host as well as the tab's. The only reach is therefore 'cause a first-party UI extension that declares onFileSystem:* to start', plus unbounded event spam. Constraining the scheme to a scheme token keeps the attacker from forging a composite activation-event string and bounds the spam alphabet; it does not need a URI check because no URI is involved.
MainThreadFileSystem.$ensureActivation.activation_blocking: yes for the public API call, no for activation: ExtHostFileSystemConsumer awaits it inside workspace.fs.stat/readFile/readDirectory/writeFile whenever the scheme has a provider in this host (`await that._proxy.$ensureActivation(uri.scheme)`, src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostFileSystemConsumer.ts#L46), so a rejection makes every workspace.fs call against an extension-provided scheme throw.

MainThreadFileSystem.$registerFileSystem.capability: become the window's file system provider for a caller-named scheme, serving every read, write, stat and watch the trusted side performs on that scheme
MainThreadFileSystem.$registerFileSystem.constraint: the scheme must be one this tab may own: a well-formed scheme token that is not a trusted or reserved scheme; the readonlyMessage must be an untrusted markdown string (isTrusted and supportHtml absent or false); handle and capabilities must be non-negative safe integers

validator.name: fileSystemProviderSchemeIsTabOwned
validator.args: arg0 (handle): Number.isSafeInteger and >= 0. arg1 (scheme): string, length 1..64, /^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*$/, and NOT in the reserved set {file, vscode-userdata, vscode-remote, vscode-remote-resource, vscode-file, vscode, vscode-webview, vscode-webview-resource, untitled, http, https, data, command, mailto, output, debug, inmemory, vscode-settings, extension, vscode-vfs, vscode-chat-code-block, vscode-notebook-cell}. arg2 (capabilities): Number.isSafeInteger and >= 0. arg3 (readonlyMessage), when present: a plain object whose only keys are a subset of {value, isTrusted, supportThemeIcons, supportHtml, baseUri, uris}; value must be a string of at most 1024 chars; isTrusted and supportHtml must be absent or literally false; baseUri/uris are rejected outright.
denies: any reserved scheme, so a tab cannot shadow the host disk, user-data or its own remote provider even if upstream's duplicate check were removed
scheme tokens with ':' '/' or control characters
a readonlyMessage whose isTrusted is true or an object (trusted markdown renders command: links, which execute commands and would launder the command policy)
a readonlyMessage carrying baseUri/uris
non-integer handle or capabilities
unrecognised keys in readonlyMessage

MainThreadFileSystem.$registerFileSystem.rationale: The handler constructs a RemoteFileSystemProvider which calls IFileService.registerProvider(scheme, this); upstream throws when the scheme is already registered, and a desktop window registers file and vscode-userdata at startup plus vscode-remote for its remote connection, so the obvious shadowing attempts already fail. That duplicate check is the only thing standing between a tab and the host disk provider, so the policy restates it rather than depending on it, and extends it to schemes the window has not registered yet (untitled, vscode-file, vscode-vfs) that the trusted side or the filter's own URI rule treats as benign. The readonlyMessage is the one free-form value: it is an IMarkdownString rendered by the editor, and trusted markdown carries command: links, which is a command-execution laundering route.
MainThreadFileSystem.$registerFileSystem.activation_blocking: no: ExtHostFileSystem.registerFileSystemProvider fires and forgets — `this._proxy.$registerFileSystemProvider(...).catch(err => console.error(...))` (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostFileSystem.ts#L180-L183). A rejection is swallowed; the extension keeps a Disposable that does nothing.
open_questions: The reserved set is a static list. If a future patch or upstream bump registers a new trusted scheme in the window, the list must be updated or that scheme becomes grabbable in the window between startup and registration.

MainThreadFileSystem.$unregisterProvider.capability: drop one of this host's own file system provider registrations
MainThreadFileSystem.$unregisterProvider.rationale: _fileProvider is a DisposableMap owned by this MainThreadFileSystem instance, and MainThreadFileSystem is per extension-host connection, so a handle only ever names a provider this tab registered. The worst case is a tab disabling its own provider. A handle that names nothing is a silent no-op, so there is nothing to fail closed on.
MainThreadFileSystem.$unregisterProvider.activation_blocking: no: called from the Disposable returned by registerFileSystemProvider, not awaited (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostFileSystem.ts#L217).

MainThreadFileSystem.$onFileSystemChange.capability: inject file change events into the window's file service for arbitrary resources
MainThreadFileSystem.$onFileSystemChange.constraint: every changes[i].resource must revive to vscode-remote with this tab's authority, or untitled:

validator.name: fileSystemChangeResourcesAreTabScoped
validator.args: arg0 (handle): Number.isSafeInteger and >= 0. arg1 (changes): an array of at most 10000 plain objects; each must have exactly the keys {resource, type} (cId optional); each `type` must be one of the IFileChangeType numbers 1|2|3; each `resource` must pass the same revive-and-check used for declared UriComponents positions (scheme vscode-remote with this tab's authority, or untitled:, and no cached external/fsPath form).

a resource carrying a vscode-remote authority that is not this tab
non-array arg1, arrays longer than the cap, non-object elements, unknown keys, out-of-range type values

MainThreadFileSystem.$onFileSystemChange.rationale: RemoteFileSystemProvider.$onFileSystemChange revives every dto.resource with URI.revive and fires them on the provider's onDidChangeFile; IFileService forwards them as a FileChangesEvent to every listener in the window and to the ext host via $onFileEvent. The resource is a nested URI, not a declared UriComponents parameter, so the positional URI rule never sees it. Forged file: events make trusted editors and watchers believe host files changed (reload prompts, dirty-state churn, participant runs) and are an unbounded event-spam channel. Constraining the resources to the tab's own filesystem removes the forgery without touching the legitimate path.
MainThreadFileSystem.$onFileSystemChange.activation_blocking: no: fired from the provider's onDidChangeFile subscription and not awaited (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostFileSystem.ts#L209).

Owning file: would show the tab every query string and folder path a trusted search issues and let it suppress or fabricate results; the fabricated-URI half is separately bounded by $handleFileMatch, but the query-observation half is not. vscode-remote must stay allowed: NativeExtHostSearch registers its ripgrep and internal file-search providers for Schemas.file, and the REH's uri transformer rewrites that to vscode-remote on the wire, so this is exactly how workspace search works inside a tab.

validator.name: none — the positional URI rule is sufficient

The positional rule covers it because the parameter is declared UriComponents[] and the filter's array expansion matches the consumer's per-element revive. Note the consumer also accepts an IRawFileMatch2-shaped element (anything with a `results` property) and revives its nested resource instead; such an element is not URI components, so the filter denies the whole call — fail-closed, and no legitimate caller sends that shape on this method.

validator.name: textMatchResourcesAreTabScoped
validator.args: arg0 (handle) and arg1 (session): Number.isSafeInteger and >= 0. arg2 (data): array of at most 10000 plain objects; each object's `resource` must pass the same revive-and-check as a declared UriComponents position; each object's `results`, when present, must be an array of at most 10000 plain objects whose string fields (previewText and the like) are each at most 64 KiB; reject any element that is not a plain object.

MainThreadSearch.$handleTextMatch.rationale: IRawFileMatch2 is IFileMatch<UriComponents>, and RemoteSearchProvider.handleFindMatch calls revive() on the whole object, turning the nested resource into a URI that the search view presents as an openable file. Because the URI is nested rather than a declared parameter, this is a gap the existing positional mechanism does not close: a rogue host can return file:///Users/<user>/.ssh/id_rsa with attacker-chosen preview text and have the window open it on a click. MainThreadSearch.$handleTelemetry.rationale: It calls ITelemetryService.publicLog(eventName, data) with both arguments straight from the wire, which is the same off-box channel as MainThreadTelemetry.$publicLog but without even a GDPR annotation at the call site. Our product.json sets enableTelemetry:false, so in a built app supportsTelemetry() is false and the window uses NullTelemetryService — but supportsTelemetry() also returns true whenever environmentService.isBuilt is false, so a development or test run of the fork would send. A surface that is inert only because of a product.json value and a build flag is not a surface to grant. Denying it loses nothing: it exists so extension-host search providers can report their own performance.
MainThreadSearch.$handleTelemetry.activation_blocking: no: there is no caller of $handleTelemetry in src/vs/workbench/api/common or node at this SHA; it is a declared-but-unused shape method, callable over RPC because the dispatcher resolves actor[methodName] without consulting the interface.

MainThreadWorkspace.$unregisterEditSessi.activation_blocking: no: called from the registration Disposable (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostWorkspace.ts#L996).

MainThreadWorkspace.$requestResourceTrus.capability: raise a modal trust dialog whose body is caller-supplied markdown and, if the user accepts, permanently mark a caller-chosen URI as trusted in application-shared storage
MainThreadWorkspace.$requestResourceTrus.rationale: requestResourcesTrust fires onDidInitiateResourcesTrustRequest, and the workspace contribution renders options.message verbatim as the first markdownDetails entry of a shield-iconed modal — a tab-authored sentence in the trusted dialog that asks the user to trust a folder. Accepting calls completeResourcesTrustRequest -> setUrisTrust([uri], true), which writes the trusted-folders list that WorkspaceTrustManagementService keeps in StorageScope.APPLICATION_SHARED and broadcasts via onDidChangeValue to every other window, so the grant is not confined to this tab. The uri is nested inside ResourceTrustRequestOptionsDto rather than being a declared UriComponents parameter, so the positional URI rule does not see it and a host path is nameable. A tab has no legitimate reason to ask for trust on anything: its own workspace is mounted and already trusted by construction, and ADR records that Workspace Trust is not a boundary for us. Denying blocks only vscode.workspace.requestResourceTrust, which no built-in extension in the observed set calls on a hot path.
MainThreadWorkspace.$requestResourceTrus.activation_blocking: yes for the public API call: ExtHostWorkspace.requestResourceTrust returns the proxy promise directly (`return this._proxy.$requestResourceTrust(options)`, src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostWorkspace.ts#L956-L958), so a rejection surfaces as a rejected promise to the extension. open_questions: If a tab-side feature ever genuinely needs this, the compatible shape is a prompt verdict with the message replaced by trusted text and the uri forced to the tab's own authority — not an argument validator, because the dialog text itself is the attack.

MainThreadWorkspace.$startFileSearch.capability: run a file search in the window over caller-named folders plus caller-named extra file resources
MainThreadWorkspace.$startFileSearch.constraint: the declared UriComponents parameter (position 0) must be this tab's own folder or null, AND every URI nested in options.extraFileResources and options.changedFileUris must satisfy the same rule

validator.name: fileSearchOptionsAreTabScoped
validator.args: arg0 (includeFolder): null/undefined or already covered positionally by SECLAB_URI_ARGS['MainThreadWorkspace.$startFileSearch'] = [0]. arg1 (options): must be a plain object; every own key must be in {_reason, excludePattern, includePattern, extraFileResources, expandPatterns, maxResults, maxFileSize, disregardIgnoreFiles, disregardGlobalIgnoreFiles, disregardParentIgnoreFiles, disregardExcludeSettings, disregardSearchExcludeSettings, ignoreSymlinks, ignoreGlobCase, onlyOpenEditors, changedFileUris, onlyFileScheme, filePattern, exists, sortByScore, cacheKey, shouldGlobSearch}; extraFileResources and changedFileUris, when present, must be arrays of at most 1000 elements each of which passes the same revive-and-check as a declared UriComponents position; all boolean-typed keys must be booleans; maxResults/maxFileSize must be safe integers >= 0; _reason/filePattern/cacheKey must be strings of at most 1024 chars; excludePattern/includePattern must be arrays/objects of strings only, bounded at 1000 entries and 1024 chars each.

any unrecognised options key, so an upstream-added URI-bearing option is denied rather than silently forwarded
non-object options, oversized pattern sets

MainThreadWorkspace.$startFileSearch.rationale: The folder argument is position 0 and is already constrained, and when it is null the search falls back to the window's workspace folders, which in a tab window are the tab's own. The gap is options: ICommonQueryBuilderOptions declares extraFileResources?: URI[] and changedFileUris?: URI[], revive(options) materialises them, and QueryBuilder.commonQuery filters them only against the include/exclude globs before putting them on the query. Everything else in options is a bounded primitive, so the validator is mostly a whitelist that fails closed on anything new.
MainThreadWorkspace.$startFileSearch.activation_blocking: yes for the public API call: ExtHostWorkspace.findFiles awaits it — `const result = await Promise.all(queryOptions?.map(option => this._proxy.$startFileSearch(...)))` (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostWorkspace.ts#L657). MainThreadWorkspace.$startTextSearch.capability: run a text search in the window over caller-named folders plus caller-named extra file resources, with results streamed back by the window
MainThreadWorkspace.$startTextSearch.constraint: same as $startFileSearch: declared folder at position 1 plus every URI nested in options.extraFileResources / options.changedFileUris

validator.name: textSearchOptionsAreTabScoped
validator.args: arg0 (pattern): plain object whose keys are a subset of the IPatternInfo fields; `pattern` must be a string of at most 64 KiB; isRegExp/isWordMatch/isCaseSensitive/isMultiline/isUnicode must be booleans or absent. arg1 (folder): null/undefined or covered positionally by SECLAB_URI_ARGS['MainThreadWorkspace.$startTextSearch'] = [1]. arg2 (options): the same whitelist as fileSearchOptionsAreTabScoped plus {previewOptions, fileEncoding, surroundingContext, isSmartCase, afterContext, beforeContext}, with the same nested-URI check on extraFileResources and changedFileUris. arg3 (requestId): safe integer >= 0.
denies: nested file:/vscode-userdata: URIs in options
unrecognised options keys
an unbounded regular expression source (capped at 64 KiB; catastrophic backtracking remains possible and is a dos residual, not a containment one)

MainThreadWorkspace.$startTextSearch.rationale: Same shape as $startFileSearch with the same nested-URI hole, but the payload returned to the caller is file CONTENT (match previews via $handleTextSearchResult), so a host-scoped extraFileResource would read host bytes into the tab rather than merely proving a path exists. The folder parameter is position 1 and already in SECLAB_URI_ARGS; when null it falls back to the window's (remote) workspace folders.
MainThreadWorkspace.$startTextSearch.activation_blocking: yes for the public API call: ExtHostWorkspace.findTextInFiles awaits the proxy promise and rethrows; it is not on an activation path unless an extension searches during activate().

MainThreadTask.$registerSupportedExecuti.capability: set the window's customExecutionSupported / shellExecutionSupported / processExecutionSupported context keys
MainThreadTask.$registerSupportedExecuti.constraint: each of the three arguments must be a boolean or absent

validator.name: supportedExecutionsAreBooleans
validator.args: arg0 (custom), arg1 (shell), arg2 (process): each must be exactly true, false, or absent/undefined. No other value, and no fourth argument.
denies: non-boolean values, which IContextKey.set would store verbatim and which then compare unpredictably in every `when` clause that reads these keys
extra arguments

MainThreadTask.$registerSupportedExecuti.rationale: registerSupportedExecutions only binds three context keys (and ANDs shell/process with 'not a virtual workspace'); it starts nothing and spawns nothing. A tab can therefore only make the task UI claim more or fewer execution kinds than are real, which is a presentation lie, and an outright deny would be worse: the remote host legitimately sends (true, true, true) from node/extHostTask.ts and the task contributions of ordinary extensions are gated on these keys. The constraint exists so the keys hold the type the `when` evaluator expects, which is the only way a value here can surprise a trusted consumer.
MainThreadTask.$registerSupportedExecuti.activation_blocking: no: called unawaited from the ExtHostTask constructor — `this._proxy.$registerSupportedExecutions(true)` in the base class (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTask.ts#L462) and `$registerSupportedExecutions(true, true, true)` in the node subclass (src/vs/workbench/api/node/extHostTask.ts#L55). A rejection becomes an unhandled rejection in the ext host.

MainThreadTask.$registerTaskProvider.capability: register a task provider for a caller-named task type, so the window asks this host for tasks and for resolved task definitions
MainThreadTask.$registerTaskProvider.constraint: the type must be a plain task-type identifier

validator.name: taskProviderTypeIsPlainIdentifier
validator.args: arg0 (handle): Number.isSafeInteger and >= 0. arg1 (type): string, length 1..64, matching /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]*$/.
denies: non-string or empty type
types carrying whitespace, control characters or markup, which are echoed into the task quick pick and the Tasks output channel
oversized types

MainThreadTask.$registerTaskProvider.rationale: The registration itself only puts an ITaskProvider in a per-connection map; the tasks it later returns are converted by TaskDTO.to, which drops any task whose scope does not resolve to a real workspace folder of this window, and a provided task is only executed on an explicit user action. Where it runs is decided by the task system info for the folder's scheme, which $registerTaskSystem constrains separately — so with that constraint in place a provided task runs in the tab, not on the host. What remains is presentation: a tab-authored task name and detail shown in the trusted Run Task picker. Denying would break the npm/typescript/gulp/grunt task providers, which are exactly what the ordinary session exercised.
MainThreadTask.$registerTaskProvider.activation_blocking: no: fired and not awaited from ExtHostTask.registerTaskProvider (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTask.ts#L472).
open_questions: The response path ($provideTasks / $resolveTask) is main->ext and returns attacker-shaped task DTOs that the RPC filter cannot see. TaskDTO.to is the only thing validating them.

MainThreadTask.$registerTaskSystem.capability: become the window's task-system info for a caller-named scheme: supply the URI scheme/authority tasks are resolved against, answer variable resolution, and answer executable lookup
MainThreadTask.$registerTaskSystem.constraint: the key and info.scheme must both be exactly 'vscode-remote', info.authority must be exactly this tab's authority, and info.platform must be one of the four strings upstream maps

validator.name: taskSystemIsThisTab
validator.args: arg0 (key): must be exactly the string 'vscode-remote'. arg1 (info): plain object whose only keys are {scheme, authority, platform}; scheme must be exactly 'vscode-remote'; authority must equal the injected authority for this connection (seclab+<tabId>), compared case-sensitively against the value the filter was constructed with, never against anything in the arguments; platform must be one of 'Web' | 'win32' | 'darwin' | 'linux'.
denies: key 'file', which unshifts the tab's info at the head of _taskSystemInfos.get('file') and so shadows the LOCAL extension host's task system for any file: workspace folder — _getTaskSystemInfo returns infos[0]
any authority other than this tab's, which would make uriProvider mint URIs for another tab's filesystem
an unknown platform string, which falls through to Platform.platform and silently adopts the host's quoting rules
unrecognised keys in info

MainThreadTask.$registerTaskSystem.rationale: registerTaskSystem installs three callbacks the window will trust: uriProvider mints URI.from({scheme: info.scheme, authority: info.authority, path}) for task configuration paths; resolveVariables sends the variable set to this host and feeds what comes back into IConfigurationResolverService and then into the task's command line; findExecutable returns the path TerminalTaskSystem uses as the command. abstractTaskService.registerTaskSystem has no duplicate check and unshifts non-Web infos, so a second registration for an existing key wins. Constraining key/scheme/authority to this tab reproduces exactly what node/extHostTask.ts sends for a remote host, so nothing legitimate is lost, while 'file' — the key the LOCAL host registers — becomes unreachable. A plain deny would break tasks in the tab entirely, because hasTaskSystemInfo gates _whenTaskSystemReady and therefore all task fetching.
MainThreadTask.$registerTaskSystem.activation_blocking: no: ExtHostTask.registerTaskSystem is a void call from the subclass constructor (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTask.ts#L485-L487, src/vs/workbench/api/node/extHostTask.ts#L43-L47); a rejection is an unhandled rejection and tasks never become ready in the tab.

MainThreadTerminalService.$registerProce.capability: set the window's terminalProcessSupported context key and fire onDidRegisterProcessSupport
MainThreadTerminalService.$registerProce.constraint: the argument must be a boolean

validator.name: processSupportIsBoolean
validator.args: arg0 (isSupported): must be exactly true or false; no other value and no extra arguments.
denies: non-boolean values stored into a context key that `when` clauses compare against
extra arguments

The reachable effect is enabling terminal-related `when` clauses in the window UI, and every terminal command those clauses expose is independently governed by the commands table, so this is not a path to a host pty. The base ExtHostTerminalService constructor sends it unconditionally, so denying would mean the tab's own terminal UI never enables.

MainThreadTerminalService.$registerQuick.capability: register a terminal quick-fix provider whose returned fixes can run a command line in the matched terminal, execute an arbitrary workbench command id, or open an arbitrary URI
MainThreadTerminalService.$registerQuick.rationale: parseQuickFix turns whatever this host returns into one of three action kinds, and quickFixAddon builds a lightbulb action for each: TerminalCommand fires onDidRequestRerunCommand with shouldExecute defaulting to true, so one click runs an attacker-chosen command line in the terminal the fix was offered for; VscodeCommand calls commandService.executeCommand(fix.id) with an id taken straight from the payload, which bypasses the whole command policy and is the verdict-laundering shape the RPC design already names as residual risk 1; Opener calls openerService.open(fix.uri) on a tab-chosen URI. The quick-fix addon is attached to terminal instances in the window, so the terminal a fix lands in is not necessarily the tab's. Neither the provider id nor the extensionId argument is bound to the connection, so a tab can also collide with a trusted provider id. None of this is constrainable from the registration arguments — the dangerous values arrive on the unfiltered response path. Denying costs only extension-contributed terminal quick fixes, which no extension in the observed ordinary session uses.
MainThreadTerminalService.$registerQuick.activation_blocking: no: fired and not awaited from registerTerminalQuickFixProvider (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTerminalService.ts#L826); the returned Disposable is simply inert.
