MainThreadTerminalService.$unregisterQui.rationale: _quickFixProviders is a per-connection DisposableMap keyed by the id this host supplied, so an id it never registered is a no-op. Harmless on its own, and keeping it allowed while $registerQuickFixProvider is denied simply means the unregister never finds anything.
MainThreadTerminalService.$unregisterQui.activation_blocking: no: called from the registration Disposable (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTerminalService.ts#L829).

MainThreadTerminalService.$setEnvironmen.capability: install, under a caller-named extension identifier, a persistent environment-variable mutation set that the window applies to terminals it creates
MainThreadTerminalService.$setEnvironmen.rationale: The collection is stamped with the connection's remoteAuthority, which is correct, but EnvironmentVariableService.getMergedCollection filters on that authority for the PATH variable only: for a local terminal (targetAuthority null) every non-PATH mutator from a tab-origin collection is still merged in. Variables such as BASH_ENV, ENV, NODE_OPTIONS, PYTHONSTARTUP, GIT_SSH_COMMAND or DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES are loader hooks, so that is host code execution the moment any local terminal or local pty is created in this window. persistent:true additionally writes the collection into StorageScope.WORKSPACE, so it survives a reload and is re-applied before the tab's extension host has even started. extensionIdentifier is an argument, so a tab can also overwrite or delete the local UI-side extensions' collections. No pure argument validator can fix this, because the defect is in which terminals the collection is applied to, not in the values. Denying breaks terminal environment contributions inside the tab — the git extension's askpass wiring and venv/conda activation — which matches the git-askpass item already recorded as a known XFAIL gap; the compatible fix is a trusted-side change making tab-origin collections apply only to terminals whose remoteAuthority equals the tab's, after which this can be revisited.
MainThreadTerminalService.$setEnvironmen.activation_blocking: no: _syncEnvironmentVariableCollection fires it unawaited whenever the collection mutates or is first created (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTerminalService.ts#L1047), including from getEnvironmentVariableCollection during activate(); the API call itself does not observe the rejection.

MainThreadDebugService.$registerDebugTyp.capability: make this host the debug adapter factory for a list of caller-named debug types in the window
MainThreadDebugService.$registerDebugTyp.constraint: every entry must be a well-formed debug type that an extension running in THIS tab actually contributes, per the trusted side's extension registry for this remote authority

validator.name: debugTypesAreContributedByThisTab
validator.args: arg0 (debugTypes): array of 1..64 strings, each length 1..64 matching /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]*$/, and each present in the set of debugger `type` values contributed by the extensions the window has enabled for this connection's remote authority (injected context: the trusted-side IExtensionService view of this tab's extension descriptions, never anything from the arguments).
denies: a debug type no extension in this tab contributes, which is how a tab would claim a type owned by a UI-side extension
non-array or empty arg0, oversized lists, malformed type tokens
duplicate entries beyond the cap

MainThreadDebugService.$registerDebugTyp.rationale: registerDebugAdapterFactory does debugTypes.forEach(t => this.debugAdapterFactories.set(t, launcher)) with no duplicate check, so registration is last-writer-wins and an unconstrained call lets a tab claim every debug type in the window. The factory it installs is MainThreadDebugService itself, which creates an ExtensionHostDebugAdapter — the DAP traffic is proxied into this host, nothing is spawned on the host from here — so the registration is not itself code execution. Its danger is that it makes the tab the authority for a debug session's protocol stream, and the stream is where the real reach is (see $acceptDAMessage). Denying outright would break all debugging in the tab, which is an ordinary feature and was observed. The validator re-derives the type list on the trusted side instead of trusting the one ExtHostDebugService computed from its own contributions.
MainThreadDebugService.$registerDebugTyp.activation_blocking: no: ExtHostDebugService calls it as a void proxy call at the end of its contributed-debuggers handling — `this._debugServiceProxy.$registerDebugTypes(debugTypes)` (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostDebugService.ts#L295) — and does not await it.

MainThreadDebugService.$acceptDAMessage.capability: deliver an arbitrary Debug Adapter Protocol message to the window on behalf of a debug session, including stack frames and loaded sources naming arbitrary file paths
MainThreadDebugService.$acceptDAMessage.constraint: no Source.path anywhere in the message may name a host path: each must be relative, or an absolute path/URI string that resolves to this tab's vscode-remote authority, or omitted in favour of a positive sourceReference

validator.name: debugAdapterMessageSourcePathsAreTabScoped
validator.args: arg0 (handle): Number.isSafeInteger and >= 0. arg1 (message): plain object, depth-capped at the same 200 the argument walker uses; walk exactly the Source containers upstream's convertPaths visits — event: output, loadedSource, breakpoint; request: setBreakpoints, breakpointLocations, source, gotoTargets, launchVSCode (runtime args); response: stackTrace, loadedSources, scopes, setFunctionBreakpoints, setBreakpoints, disassemble, locations — and for every container with a string `path`: accept it when `sourceReference` is a number > 0 (upstream leaves the path untouched); otherwise accept only if the path is NOT absolute per vs/base/common/path isAbsolute, or if it parses as a URI whose scheme is vscode-remote with this tab's authority.
denies: an absolute filesystem path such as /Users/<user>/.ssh/id_rsa or C:\\Users\\..., because getUriFromSource turns exactly that into URI.file(path) — a host file URI that the debug UI opens in an editor of this window when the session stops or the user clicks a frame, and a document opened in a tab window is synchronised back into the tab
a URI string with scheme file:, vscode-userdata: or a foreign vscode-remote authority
messages deeper than the walker cap, rather than guessing

MainThreadDebugService.$acceptDAMessage.rationale: MainThreadDebugService.$acceptDAMessage pipes the message through convertToVSCPaths(message, false), whose uriToString leaves string paths alone, and the debug model then builds Source via getUriFromSource, which resolves an absolute path with URI.file and an isUriString path with URI.parse — neither of which carries the session's remote authority. Source.openInEditor opens that URI with the window's editor service. The Source containers are nested deep inside the DAP payload, so no declared UriComponents position exists and the positional rule cannot see them. This is the method where the debug surface actually reaches the host filesystem, which is why $registerDebugTypes can be constrained rather than denied.
MainThreadDebugService.$acceptDAMessage.activation_blocking: no: sent from the debug adapter's onMessage handler — `mythis._debugServiceProxy.$acceptDAMessage(debugAdapterHandle, message)` (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostDebugService.ts#L682) — unawaited.
open_questions: Upstream appears to convert remote debug sources to host file: URIs as well (the ext host makes a file: URI, the main thread turns it back into an fsPath string, and Source re-files it). If so, constraining to vscode-remote may reject paths an honest remote debug adapter sends; the fallback is to accept absolute paths only by rewriting them onto this tab's authority rather than denying.

MainThreadTunnelService.$setRemoteTunnel.capability: name this host's process id to the remote explorer and switch on the port-candidate finding loop for the window
MainThreadTunnelService.$setRemoteTunnel.rationale: It records the caller-supplied pid in remoteExplorerService.namedProcesses and then drives $registerCandidateFinder, which asks this host to report host:port candidates that the window's auto-forward logic consumes and opens tunnels for; MainThreadTunnelService.$openTunnel already carries a prompt verdict for exactly that reason, and turning the candidate loop on from inside the sandbox would feed it. The pid is an argument and is only used as a label, so there is no identity value in it either. Keeping the existing deny loses automatic port-forward detection inside a tab, which is a convenience the broker design does not rely on: the tab's only egress is its own broker.
MainThreadTunnelService.$setRemoteTunnel.activation_blocking: no: called from the NodeExtHostTunnelService constructor, unawaited and only on Linux remotes — `this._proxy.$setRemoteTunnelService(process.pid)` (src/vs/workbench/api/node/extHostTunnelService.ts#L195).

MainThreadUrls.$registerUriHandler.capability: claim the OS protocol-URL handler for a caller-named extension identifier in this window
MainThreadUrls.$registerUriHandler.rationale: extensionId is an RPC argument, and ExtensionUrlHandler.handleURL authorises purely by comparing it with uri.authority — so a tab that claims 'vscode.github-authentication' receives every seclab-vscode://vscode.github-authentication/... URL the OS routes to this window, which is how an OAuth redirect delivers its authorization code. ExtensionUrlHandlerImpl.registerExtensionHandler is a plain Map.set keyed by the extension id, so the claim overwrites the real UI-side provider's entry, and AbstractURLService.open walks all registered handlers taking the first that returns true. Protocol URLs are dispatched by the main process to a window the user did not choose, so the interception is not even confined to flows the tab started. This directly violates the no-real-secret-in-a-tab invariant, and the identity it depends on comes from arguments, which the identity-never-from-arguments invariant forbids. Denying costs vscode.window.registerUriHandler for tab extensions; nothing in the observed ordinary session needs it to function, and a tab has no business receiving host protocol URLs at all.
MainThreadUrls.$registerUriHandler.activation_blocking: no: ExtHostUrls.registerUriHandler fires the call and returns a Disposable without awaiting (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostUrls.ts#L40).

MainThreadUrls.$unregisterUriHandler.capability: drop one of this host's own URL handler registrations
MainThreadUrls.$unregisterUriHandler.rationale: The handle is looked up in this connection's own handlers map; an unknown handle returns early. With $registerUriHandler denied the map is always empty, so the call is inert, but allowing it keeps the extension's Disposable from producing an unhandled rejection.
MainThreadUrls.$unregisterUriHandler.activation_blocking: no: called from the registration Disposable (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostUrls.ts#L45).

MainThreadWindow.$getInitialState.capability: read two booleans about this window: whether it has focus and whether the user is active
MainThreadWindow.$getInitialState.rationale: It returns only hostService.hasFocus and userActivityService.isActive for this window — no path, no identity, no host configuration. The same facts are pushed into the host continuously and unfilterably by the constructor's $onDidChangeWindowFocus and $onDidChangeWindowActive subscriptions, so denying the initial read buys nothing and only leaves vscode.window.state wrong until the first change event. The honest residual is that a tab can time activity for when the user is away, which it can do regardless of this verdict.
MainThreadWindow.$getInitialState.activation_blocking: no: ExtHostWindow's constructor calls it with .then() and never awaits — `this._proxy.$getInitialState().then(({ isFocused, isActive }) => ...)` (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostWindow.ts#L56-L59). A rejection would be an unhandled rejection at ext-host startup, which is itself a reason not to deny a method with no reach.

MainThreadTelemetry.$publicLog2.capability: emit a telemetry event with a caller-chosen name and arbitrary properties through the window's telemetry service
MainThreadTelemetry.$publicLog2.rationale: $publicLog2 is a thin typed wrapper that calls $publicLog, which tags the data and hands it to ITelemetryService.publicLog with both arguments straight from the wire. In our build product.json sets enableTelemetry:false, so for a built app supportsTelemetry() is false and the native workbench TelemetryService installs NullTelemetryService — the call is inert there. It is not inert in general: supportsTelemetry() returns true whenever environmentService.isBuilt is false unless --disable-telemetry is passed, so any development or test run of the fork sends, and the only thing standing between a tab and an off-box channel would be one product.json boolean that no invariant pins. Telemetry leaving the box is explicitly unacceptable in this threat model, so the surface is denied rather than left conditionally inert. Denying costs nothing a tab needs: ExtHostTelemetry's own API already honours the telemetry level it is told about.
MainThreadTelemetry.$publicLog2.activation_blocking: no: every caller is fire-and-forget on a void shape method, e.g. ExtHostWorkspace's findFiles instrumentation `this._telemetryProxy.$publicLog2<FindFilesEvent, ...>('extHostFindFiles', event)` (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostWorkspace.ts#L718) and the API-deprecation reporter (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostApiDeprecationService.ts#L57).

MainThreadTelemetry.$publicLog.capability: the untyped form of the same event emission; $publicLog2 delegates to it
MainThreadTelemetry.$publicLog.rationale: Same implementation and the same reasoning: eventName and data are both attacker-controlled and go to ITelemetryService.publicLog. Denying $publicLog2 while allowing $publicLog would leave the identical channel open, since the typing exists only in TypeScript and the RPC dispatcher resolves actor[methodName] without consulting the interface.
MainThreadTelemetry.$publicLog.activation_blocking: no: no awaited caller; it is a void shape method.

MainThreadChatSkills.$getTools.capability: enumerate every language-model tool registered in the window, including disabled ones, with their ids, descriptions, tags, source and full JSON input schemas
MainThreadChatSkills.$getTools.rationale: getToolDtos maps getAllToolsIncludingDisabled() — the whole window-wide registry, which includes tools contributed by the trusted UI-side extensions and by the workbench itself — into DTOs carrying modelDescription, inputSchema and source. That is a complete map of the trusted agent surface handed to a sandboxed host: exactly the reconnaissance a tab would use to pick a laundering target, and the same reason MainThreadCommands.$getCommands is filtered rather than allowed. Built-in chat is disabled inside tabs by a separate patch, so an empty answer is also the honest one; denying leaves ExtHostLanguageModelTools._allTools empty and vscode.lm.tools reporting nothing, which is the intended state for a tab.
MainThreadChatSkills.$getTools.activation_blocking: no: the ExtHostLanguageModelTools constructor calls it with .then() and never awaits — `this._proxy.$getTools().then(tools => {...})` (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageModelTools.ts#L91-L95). A rejection is an unhandled rejection at ext-host startup, not an activation failure.
open_questions: The sid on the wire is 'MainThreadChatSkills' even though the class and the MainContext property are MainThreadLanguageModelTools; the policy key must stay the sid.

MainThreadChatSkills.$registerTool.capability: supply the implementation for a caller-named tool id in the window's language-model tool registry
MainThreadChatSkills.$registerTool.rationale: registerToolImplementation binds an id taken from the arguments to an invoke/prepareToolInvocation/handleToolStream triple that calls back into this host. The id is not checked against anything the tab contributed, so a tab can supply the body of a tool a trusted-side extension declared, and then answer whatever a model-driven agent on the trusted side asks it — including prepareToolInvocation, which drives the confirmation UI the user reads before approving a tool run. Chat is disabled in tabs, so nothing legitimate is lost; this is denied as the write counterpart of $getTools rather than as a separate judgement.
MainThreadChatSkills.$registerTool.activation_blocking: no: a void shape method called from ExtHostLanguageModelTools.registerTool without await.

MainThreadLogger.$registerLogger.capability: add a logger resource to the window's logger service, making a caller-named URI a known logger
MainThreadLogger.$registerLogger.rationale: Keep denied, as the rpc-filter-log-is-trustworthy invariant requires: the filter's own decision log is written through ILoggerService, and registering a logger for a URI is the step that makes $log able to append to it later, so the deny on this method is half of the reason $log cannot forge lines in the filter's evidence. The resource is nested inside the ILoggerResource DTO rather than being a declared UriComponents position for this method, so the positional URI rule would not even see it. Denying blocks the window-side half of vscode.window.createOutputChannel(name, {log: true}) for tab extensions: the logger still exists inside the REH and still writes its file there, but the channel does not appear in the window's Output picker. No activation and no extension API call fails as a result.
MainThreadLogger.$registerLogger.activation_blocking: no: ExtHostLoggerService.registerLogger calls it after the local registration and does not await — `this._proxy.$registerLogger(resource)` (src/vs/workbench/api/node/extHostLoggerService.ts#L25).

MainThreadLogger.$createLogger.capability: create a logger in the window for a caller-named URI, which is the prerequisite $log checks before appending
MainThreadLogger.$createLogger.rationale: Keep denied under the same pinned invariant. $createLogger takes a declared UriComponents parameter (position 0 is in SECLAB_URI_ARGS), so the positional rule would already confine it to the tab's own authority — but a logger whose resource is inside the tab is still a logger the window's logger service owns and writes, and the invariant's argument is that no tab may influence the log the filter's evidence is read from. In the remote case ExtHostLoggerService.doCreateLogger builds the file logger inside the extension host for file: resources anyway, specifically to keep this traffic off the IPC channel, so denying the window-side create costs only the Output-panel view of that log.
MainThreadLogger.$createLogger.activation_blocking: no: called without await from the base ExtHostLoggerService when a logger is created.

MainThreadLogger.$deregisterLogger.capability: remove a logger registration from the window by URI
MainThreadLogger.$deregisterLogger.rationale: Keep denied. Unlike the per-connection handle maps elsewhere, ILoggerService is keyed by resource URI and is window-wide, so a deregister names a logger by name rather than by something bound to the caller; with the whole MainThreadLogger surface denied there is nothing to deregister anyway. Denying costs only the tidy-up half of a logger lifecycle that never started on the window side.
MainThreadLogger.$deregisterLogger.activation_blocking: no: called without await from ExtHostLoggerService.deregisterLogger (src/vs/workbench/api/node/extHostLoggerService.ts#L28-L31).

MainThreadCommands.$fireCommandActivatio.capability: make the window activate extensions by the activation event onCommand:<caller-chosen id>, in every extension host including the trusted local one
MainThreadCommands.$fireCommandActivatio.constraint: the id must be one this tab could legitimately be executing: an id this tab registered through $registerCommand, or an id whose commands-table verdict for this tab is allow or prompt

validator.name: commandActivationIdIsTabReachable
validator.args: arg0 (id): string, length 1..255, no control characters; must be either present in the set of command ids this connection registered via $registerCommand (filter-side bookkeeping, not an argument), or resolve in the commands table to a verdict other than deny for this tab. The seclab. prefix is refused before the table is consulted, as everywhere else.
denies: ids the tab may not execute, which is how it would drive activation of a first-party UI-side extension (the Tab Manager, an auth provider) at a moment of its choosing
ids carrying control characters, which end up concatenated into an activation-event string
unbounded id lengths used as activation-event spam

MainThreadCommands.$fireCommandActivatio.rationale: The method prefixes the id with onCommand: and calls IExtensionService.activateByEvent, which is the window's extension service and therefore spans both extension hosts; a tab can thus start a trusted UI-side extension and observe the timing. It is guarded by activationEventIsDone, so repeats are cheap, but the first call per id is not. Denying it outright would be wrong: ExtHostCommands fires it on every in-host command execution, so the tab's own commands would stop emitting their activation events and extensions that lazily register handlers would break. Binding the id to what the tab may already execute leaves the legitimate case intact.
MainThreadCommands.$fireCommandActivatio.activation_blocking: no, and deliberately so: ExtHostCommands fires it immediately before running the in-host command and the upstream comment says it is not awaited — `this.#proxy.$fireCommandActivationEvent(id); return this._executeContributedCommand<T>(id, args, false);` (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostCommands.ts#L185-L186).

MainThreadCommands.$unregisterCommand.constraint: only ids this tab registered — which upstream already guarantees, so the validator is defence in depth and a place to fail closed

validator.name: tabCommandUnregistration
validator.args: arg0 (id): string, length 1..255, and present in this connection's own set of ids previously accepted by $registerCommand (the same filter-side bookkeeping commandActivationIdIsTabReachable uses). No second argument.
denies: ids the tab never registered, including the trusted ids in SECLAB_TRUSTED_COMMAND_IDS, so the verdict does not depend on upstream keeping its registrations per host
non-string or oversized ids

MainThreadCommands.$unregisterCommand.rationale: _commandRegistrations is a DisposableMap on MainThreadCommands, and MainThreadCommands is instantiated per extension-host connection, so deleteAndDispose can only reach a registration this same tab made: an id it never registered is a silent no-op, and a trusted command registered by the workbench or by a UI-side extension is in a different instance's map entirely. The reachable effect is therefore self-DoS, plus the narrow case of a tab releasing an id it had shadowed, which restores the original registration rather than removing it. The existing policy entry already says 'only ids this tab registered'; this records that upstream enforces it structurally, and keeps the validator so the guarantee survives an upstream refactor. Note the existing entry's evidence cites L81-L93, which is $executeCommand; the correct range is L68-L70.
MainThreadCommands.$unregisterCommand.activation_blocking: no: called from the Disposable returned by registerCommand, only when the command was registered globally, and not awaited (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostCommands.ts#L163-L170).

MainThreadStorage.$registerExtensionStor.capability: declare which global-state keys of a caller-named extension id and version Settings Sync should upload
MainThreadStorage.$registerExtensionStor.rationale: setKeysForSync writes extensionKeys/<id>@<version> into StorageScope.PROFILE, which is shared by every window on the profile, and the extension identity is taken entirely from the arguments — so a tab can nominate another extension's keys, including a UI-side auth provider's memento keys, and have Settings Sync carry their values off the machine. That is both the identity-never-from-arguments violation and a direct exfiltration channel, and it is cross-window because the storage scope is not the tab's. Denying only loses the sync of a tab extension's own global state, which is behaviour we do not want anyway; no API call fails.
MainThreadStorage.$registerExtensionStor.activation_blocking: no: ExtHostStorage.registerExtensionStorageKeysToSync is a void proxy call behind context.globalState.setKeysForSync (src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostStorage.ts#L35-L37).

MainThreadStorage.$initializeExtensionSt.capability: read the raw stored state of a caller-named extension id, and subscribe this host to changes of it
MainThreadStorage.$initializeExtensionSt.rationale: extensionId is an argument and is used directly as the storage key, so a tab can read any extension's memento — including UI-side extensions' — and, for shared (global) state, register to be pushed every later change through $acceptValue. It also runs checkAndMigrateExtensionStorage, which can move another extension's state. This is the same identity-from-arguments defect the MainThreadSecretState entries resolve with a rewrite, and the same resolution applies here: discard the argument and use the connection-bound identity, partitioned per tab. Recorded as deny because deny is the fail-closed placeholder, but deny is genuinely breaking — ExtensionMemento awaits it, so every tab extension's globalState/workspaceState would be empty or failed; this should land as a rewrite, not a deny.
MainThreadStorage.$initializeExtensionSt.activation_blocking: yes: ExtHostStorage.initializeExtensionStorage awaits the proxy call (`const value = await this._proxy.$initializeExtensionStorage(shared, key)`, src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostStorage.ts#L39-L40) and ExtensionMemento's whenReady is awaited before an extension's activate() is called, so a rejection fails activation of every extension in the tab.
open_questions: Should be classified as rewrite (rebind to the connection identity, partition by tab) together with $setValue; the deny here is a placeholder, not a recommendation to ship.

MainThreadStorage.$setValue.capability: write the stored state of a caller-named extension id
MainThreadStorage.$setValue.rationale: The key argument is the extension id and is passed straight to setExtensionState, so a tab can overwrite another extension's memento — poisoning a UI-side extension's persisted state or destroying it. Same identity-from-arguments shape and same rewrite resolution as $initializeExtensionStorage; deny is the fail-closed placeholder and breaks Memento.update for tab extensions.
MainThreadStorage.$setValue.activation_blocking: no for activation, yes for the API call: ExtensionMemento.update returns the awaited setValue promise, so a rejection surfaces to the extension.
open_questions: Same as $initializeExtensionStorage: the compatible verdict is rewrite.

cross_cutting: Nested URIs are the recurring gap. The positional SECLAB_URI_ARGS mechanism only sees parameters declared as UriComponents in extHost.protocol.ts. Five methods in this group carry URIs the consumer revives from inside objects or DTOs and that the positional rule therefore never inspects: MainThreadSearch.$handleTextMatch (data[].resource), MainThreadFileSystem.$onFileSystemChange (changes[].resource), MainThreadWorkspace.$requestResourceTrust (options.uri), MainThreadWorkspace.$startFileSearch and $startTextSearch (options.extraFileResources, options.changedFileUris), and MainThreadDebugService.$acceptDAMessage (every DAP Source.path). Any validator written for these should reuse the filter's existing _checkUriComponents, including its cached-external/fsPath check, rather than re-deriving a URI test.

Scheme-keyed registries decide who the window trusts, and they do not agree with each other about duplicates. IFileService.registerProvider throws on a duplicate scheme; ISearchService.registerSearchResultProvider silently overwrites; IDebugAdapterManager.registerDebugAdapterFactory silently overwrites; AbstractTaskService.registerTaskSystem unshifts so the newest non-Web entry wins; ExtensionUrlHandlerImpl.registerExtensionHandler is a plain Map.set. Policy for every register* method in this group is therefore written as 'which names may this tab claim', not 'upstream will stop a collision'.

Identity taken from arguments appears again outside MainThreadSecretState: MainThreadUrls.$registerUriHandler (extensionId), MainThreadTerminalService.$setEnvironmentVariableCollection (extensionIdentifier), MainThreadStorage.$registerExtensionStorageKeysToSync / $initializeExtensionStorage / $setValue (extension id). The identity-never-from-arguments invariant applies to all of them; three are denied here and the storage trio really wants the same rewrite treatment MainThreadSecretState received.

Three surfaces in this group launder past the commands table without going through $executeCommand: a terminal quick fix of type VscodeCommand (commandService.executeCommand(fix.id)), a trusted IMarkdownString rendered from a tab-supplied readonlyMessage or dialog message (command: links), and anything else that renders tab markdown as trusted. These are instances of the already-recorded deferred-laundering residual, and each is handled here by denying or by forcing isTrusted false.

Several verdicts depend on state the filter does not hold today: the tab's contributed debug types and its extension set (debugTypesAreContributedByThisTab), and the set of command ids this connection registered (commandActivationIdIsTabReachable, tabCommandUnregistration). The last one is filter-side bookkeeping that $registerCommand can maintain cheaply; the debug one needs a read of the trusted-side extension registry scoped to this remote authority. Neither may ever be derived from call arguments.

Main->ext pushes are outside this filter and some of them undo part of what is argued above: MainThreadFileSystemEventService's constructor forwards every uncorrelated file change in the window to the host via $onFileEvent regardless of $watch; MainThreadWindow pushes focus and activity changes continuously; MainThreadTask calls $resolveVariables and $findExecutable into the host and then trusts the answers. Verdicts here should not be read as containing those paths.

Telemetry is inert in this build only because product.json sets enableTelemetry:false and supportsTelemetry() short-circuits for built apps. The same function returns true for any non-built run. Both MainThreadTelemetry.$publicLog/$publicLog2 and MainThreadSearch.$handleTelemetry are denied rather than relying on that, and a product.json invariant pinning enableTelemetry would be worth adding independently.

Correction to an existing entry: policy.json's MainThreadCommands.$unregisterCommand cites mainThreadCommands.ts#L81-L93, which is $executeCommand. The correct range is L68-L70. The substance of the entry is right and is in fact stronger than stated, because _commandRegistrations is per extension-host connection.
